newsitem.title: FRANCE: Swiss Cargo to develop Brussels cargo hub.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Cargo to develop Brussels cargo hub.

text.p: Swiss Cargo, the cargo arm of Swissair, said it planned to develop Brussels airport as its cargo hub in northern Europe as part of its global alliance with Belgian airline, Sabena.
In October 1996, Swissair announced it would be marketing Sabena total cargo capacity, effective January 1 1997.
The hub will serve air cargo markets in Scandinavia, the Benelux and the UK.

"We envisage operating full-freighter flights from Brussels to long-haul destinations as we do currently from Basle and Geneva, using traffic rights already accorded to Sabena but which they do not utilise," a Swiss Cargo official told Reuters.
Swissair operates a twice-weekly full -freighter service between Geneva and Singapore with stopovers at Dubai and Madras, using a wet-leased 65-tonne capacity McDonnell Douglas DC10-30F aircraft.
It also operates a weekly full-freighter service between Geneva and Sao Paulo using the same type of aircraft.

Swissair also operates a weekly McDonnell Douglas DC10F service between Basel and Chicago, a weekly DC8F service between Basle and Atlanta and a weekly Boeing 747F service linking Basle and Seoul in conjunction with Korean Air.
"From Brussels, our aim is to have a number of full-freighter flights in service, with a start-up during the course of 1997 although these plans have yet to be finalised."
Priority destinations included Hong Kong, Tokyo, Shangai, Buenos Aires and New York, the official added.
"Our customers will benefit from improved access to a global air cargo network, an increase in the number of flights, and from the proposed expansion of our freight operations."

"For example, in the UK, where Swissair reduced its cargo capacity in replacing palletised Airbus 310 passenger aircraft with Airbus 320s and 321s, forwarders will have an all-cargo option to long-haul destinations from Brussels via an ex-London trucking link, the official said.
"More details on the development of Swiss Cargo northern Europe hub and its plans for all-cargo services, will probably emerge following a meeting of its cargo managers in Brussels next week."
Swissair said its cooperation with Sabena will increase its annual cargo capacity from 1.6 billion FTK to close to two billion FTK.
Since January 1 1997 all Sabena freight travels under Swissair air way bills.
Swissair's cargo division, now trading as Swiss Cargo became an independent bsuiness unit on January 1 1997. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax +44-171-542-5017
